input: Our SoC has ARM RAS v2 extensions. We're seeing EDAC reports of correctable L3 ECC errors increasing over time — about 50 per hour now. The rasdaemon SQLite database shows errors clustered on one L3 slice. At what point do correctable errors become a reliability concern? Should we proactively offline memory pages before an uncorrectable error occurs? How does the Linux memory poisoning (HWPoison) mechanism interact with RAS FHIR?
